s1.syndrome_frame: Acute unilateral ocular inflammation with vision loss
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber
Mild nuclear sclerosis
Whitish focal granuloma at the 4-o'clock position at the pupillary margin
Posterior segment was unremarkable
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods in a branching pattern
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute unilateral ocular inflammation with vision loss
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber
Mild nuclear sclerosis
Whitish focal granuloma at the 4-o'clock position at the pupillary margin
Posterior segment was unremarkable
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods in a branching pattern
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius

differentials: Iridocyclitis associated with inflammatory bowel disease
per_call: Iridocyclitis associated with inflammatory bowel disease

shortlist.label: Endogenous bacterial endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain and culture results indicate bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, a type of streptococcal bacteria

shortlist.label: Acute anterior uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with conjunctival hyperemia, keratic precipitates, and 3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber

shortlist.label: Endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of hypopyon and increased fibrinous material emanating from the iris lesion

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, toxoplasmosis can cause ocular inflammation and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's recent dental cleaning, lack of ocular history, and presence of gram-positive cocci in chains (Streptococcus intermedius) in the gram stain, along with the clinical presentation of decreased visual acuity, conjunctival hyperemia, keratic precipitates, and a whitish focal granuloma, support the diagnosis of endogenous bacterial endophthalmitis.

rejected.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
rejected.why: While Streptococcus intermedius was identified, this option is too specific and does not fully capture the complexity of the presentation.

rejected.label: Acute anterior uveitis
rejected.why: The presence of a whitish focal granuloma and the identification of bacteria suggest a more severe infection than uveitis alone.

rejected.label: Endophthalmitis
rejected.why: This option is too broad and does not specify the bacterial cause, which is a key aspect of the diagnosis.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence to support this diagnosis, such as characteristic retinochoroiditis or a positive toxoplasma serology.
